Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our security and platform teams reviewed Redwood's private control plane offering and we have a few integration items to lock down before procurement will sign off:

- SAML: we need a clear assertion contract (attributes, NameID format, groups → role claim mapping, recommended session TTLs). We also want a description of how assertions are validated (cert rotation expectations, allowed issuers).
- SCIM: we'd like to understand trade-offs for (1) Greenline-run SCIM endpoint that Redwood pulls from, (2) Greenwood-managed push (Redwood SCIM client), and (3) hybrid (read-only sync + manual enrollment). We care about provisioning resiliency and delta handling.
- Delegated admin: our ops team prefers a model where operator-level accounts are JIT-provisioned and can be revoked by Greenline admins without Redwood intervention.
- Audit: retention policy and where logs live; we need to know if audit exports can be sent to our SIEM.

Attached is a short requirements doc (Greenline-idp-requirements.pdf). Can you outline a recommended pattern and any contract/legal items we should expect? Procurement and legal will join once we have a draft.

Sarah — great to hear from you. High level: we support flexible assertion contracts and three SCIM modes; the right choice depends on your security posture and ops preferences. Quick summary below and I've attached a compact contract + provisioning options sheet.

1) SAML assertion contract (recommended pattern)
   - Required attributes: email (NameID, persistent), sub, exp, iat
   - Optional: groups claim (array, up to 512 entries), department, role_hint
   - Recommended NameID: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:unspecified (email)
   - Signing: IdP-signed assertions + metadata URL for cert rotation. We rotate our SP certs on a 12-month cadence; recommend customer keep an overlap window for metadata changes.

2) SCIM modes
   - Mode A (Customer-managed SCIM endpoint): Redwood pulls; best for strict customer control and for customers with existing provisioning systems.
   - Mode B (Redwood-managed push): Redwood acts as SCIM client; requires a Redwood service account on your side. Easier for customers that want Redwood to proactively create operator accounts.
   - Mode C (Hybrid/manual): SCIM for groups + manual role binding for high-privilege operators. Best when you want tight review before granting elevated rights.

3) Delegated admin / JIT pattern
   - We can JIT-provision operator accounts on first SAML login and map to temporary operator roles with TTL (configurable, default 7 days).
   - Revocation: group claim removal + SCIM deprovision event triggers immediate demotion; for immediate emergency revocation we support a customer-controlled blocklist via our control-plane API.

4) Audit & log export
   - Audit events retained 90 days by default; extended retention is an add-on. Logs can be exported to your S3 or streamed to a SIEM via our log-forwarder (TLS + customer key).

Attachments: redwood-saml-assertion-contract-v1.pdf, redwood-scim-options.xlsx, MAP stub. I also added a short mutual action plan link: https://redwood.app/s/PRIVCP-MAP-GL-9082

Adding operational notes from an operator perspective:

- JIT operator creation: we should enforce short TTLs by default (7d) and surface token expiry in the UI. For long-running tasks, operators should request extension via Greenline admin approval that triggers an audit event.
- SCIM delta handling: recommend a last-write-wins model but also provide an option for soft-deletes ("suspend") so accidental deletes don't immediately revoke access.
- RBAC vs ABAC: we recommend RBAC for PrivCP operator roles and reserve ABAC-style attribute checks for temporary policy guards (e.g., time-of-day or IP). Keep role bindings simple (group ID → role).
- Legal/data retention: from a compliance standpoint, Greenline may ask for a contract clause limiting PII retention in audit logs. Laura/legal should propose default language (we've used 90-day retention + customer-requested export earlier).

Operational ask: can the SCIM client support PATCH deltas and incremental syncing rather than full resyncs? That reduces downtime during large changes.

— Vanessa
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — here's a concise rollout proposal and deliverables we can present to Greenline legal/procurement:

Phase 0 — Discovery (1 week)
  - Confirm NameID (email vs employee_id), group claim format, and cert rotation windows.
  - Pick SCIM mode (A/B/C) and define the provisioning endpoint/credentials.

Phase 1 — Contract & Assertion Mapping (1 week)
  - Produce a signed SAML assertion contract, with examples and a test metadata exchange.
  - Draft an addendum for audit retention (default 90 days, option to extend).

Phase 2 — PoC (2–3 weeks)
  - PoC in Greenline staging: SAML assertion tests, SCIM sync validation, JIT provisioning test, SIEM forwarder verification.
  - Deliverable: PoC report + remediation list.

Phase 3 — Staged Cutover (1 week)
  - Canary group, monitor for auth failures, rollback plan (switch to read-only role mapping).

Phase 4 — Post-cutover validation (2 weeks)
  - Run regression evals on sign-in flows, role expirations, and audit exports.

  - Laura: prep contract addendum language for legal + MAP doc.
